class.name: NetwInterestDelta
class.brief_description: What one [method NetwInterestEngine.recompute] produced: the rows that move, and the per-peer edges that opened and closed.
class.description: A value handed out by [method NetwInterestEngine.recompute] and handed back to [method NetwInterestEngine.commit]. Between those two calls the engine's read matrix is untouched, which is what lets a caller decide what a transition means before acting on it. Whatever [method NetwInterestEngine.commit] needs to advance the read matrix rides inside this value and is nobody else's business, so it is not on the bound surface: a caller reading a transition never needs the state the engine is about to replace its own with. [codeblock] keys ┄ old_rows ┄ new_rows ┄ order_keys parallel, one entry per moved row shows ┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄ [entity, bit] ordered parent-first hides ┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄┄ [entity, bit] ordered child-first layer_shows/hides [layer, entity, bit] the same edges, attributed removed_keys ┄┄┄┄ entities that left their last row is a hide [/codeblock] The two orderings are the point rather than a detail: hides run child before parent and shows run parent before child, so no peer ever holds a child whose parent it cannot see, in either direction. [member layer_shows] and [member layer_hides] answer which layer an edge is owed to, and they diff memberships as well as rows. Joining a layer that already admitted a peer attributes that edge without the entity's own row moving at all.

method.name: is_empty
method.description: Whether no row moved. A pass over unchanged state answers [code]true[/code].

method.name: to_array
method.description: Every field as one array of plain values, for comparing two passes against each other.
